metadata.title: BenVaSim Stage 1 / Model 1.1(a): 1D HM-coupled saturated column (Biot consolidation benchmark)

source.journal: Synthesis report, BMWi joint research project BenVaSim (02E11567A-B), TU Clausthal

metadata.validation_method: analytical solution (transient + steady state), Lux et al. (2021)
metadata.validation_target: Pore-pressure evolution at X=0.25/0.75/1.25/5/9.75 m and lhs displacement over 30 a
metadata.notes: v5 (2026-08-17): LATERAL CONFINEMENT ADDED - the fix for the v4 'pipeline storage bug', which was a MISDIAGNOSIS. v4 clamped uy only on edge_bottom, leaving the top edge y=0.5 traction-free, and argued that nu=0 makes the transverse direction inert. That is true for pure mechanics but FALSE under Biot coupling: sigma_yy = M*eps_yy - b*p, so a free top gives eps_yy = b*p/M regardless of nu. Consequences measured on the 2026-08-16 run: undrained jump p_u = sigma/(2+E/Q) = 3.4949e5 Pa instead of the 1D sigma/(1+E/Q) = 5.7181e5 Pa (ratio 0.6112, predicted 0.6111); u_lhs/L = 6.8633e-5 instead of 4.086e-5 = exactly (sigma-p_u)/E; and the top edge really moved, uy = 2.184e-5 m = (p_u/E)*0.5 to 4 digits. Momentum was exact (E*eps+p = 898559 vs 898700 Pa), so load, moduli and coupling were all correct - only the kinematic BC was wrong. The v4 fingerprint S_used = eps_xx/p = 1.9638e-10 = 1/Q + b^2/E is what you get when you invert the storage from eps_xx ALONE while eps_yy is free; there is NO spurious b^2/M in the assembly and no OOFEM source change is warranted. Second symptom of the same cause: a spurious 2D near-field at the pressure boundary (at 30 a, x=0.25 m read 787001 Pa at y=0 vs 668015 Pa at y=0.5) decaying over ~0.5 m = one strip height, with the probes at y=0.25 sitting inside it. Also raised dt_min 1e3 -> 6e3 s to clear the upquad11 monotonicity floor dt >= h^2/(6c) = 0.0415^2/(6*5.09e-8) = 5.6e3 s; v4 rang on both boundaries at step 1 (29 nodes undershooting the interior plateau). Full evidence in ANALYSIS.md. v4: results{} rewired onto reference data digitised from the report's Figs 4.7-4.11 (see reference/README.md). PLOT UNITS ARE THE REPORT'S OWN: absolute MPa and years, not excess Pa - simulation curves carry scale/offset to match, references need none. NOTE reference/transient_probes.csv is EMPTY (header only); the old an_transient ref pointed at it, so the transient plot and console.reference_deviation were silently comparing against nothing. Both now use the digitised Fig. 4.8 analytical curves. v3: line_profile start/end now 2 coordinates (backend requirement); displacement sign corrected - compaction is positive, lhs moves toward the clamped end, u_lhs ss = +5.617e-4 m. v2: added displacement.rho (required by builder; quasi-static -> no physical effect); probes as dim-0 groups for exact nodes. 1D model mapped to 2D plane strain; nu=0 makes M=E, so the mapping is EXACT (Sec. 2.2) PROVIDED eps_yy is suppressed by clamping BOTH lateral edges. Pressures are EXCESS values relative to the 0.1013 MPa initial datum (exact shift). No 1-day BC ramp available (BGR/ENSI used one) - expect small early-time boundary oscillations, as observed in the report itself (Fig. 4.9). Equal-order u/p: check pressure profile for checkerboarding near t=0+.

entities._comment: PAPER_VALUE: 10 m column length (Sec. 4.1.1). ASSUMED: 0.1 m transverse width = TWO elements at element_size 0.05. The 1D model has no transverse dimension and, with both lateral edges clamped in uy, eps_yy=0, so the width has zero physical effect - it is pure DOF cost. Was 0.5 m (10 elements) until v6. NOT 0.05 m (one element): gmsh's Blossom recombination needs an EVEN number of divisions on every boundary curve and fails with '1D mesh cannot be divided by 2', so two elements is the minimum for a quad mesh.

physical_groups.name: edge_bottom
physical_groups._comment: Lower lateral edge. Clamped in uy together with edge_top to enforce the 1D oedometric kinematics eps_yy=0. NOTE the v4 comment here was wrong: 'nu=0 so it does not perturb the x-solution' holds for pure mechanics only - see metadata.notes.

physical_groups.name: edge_top
physical_groups._comment: Upper lateral edge, added in v5. Must be clamped in uy: leaving it traction-free lets the Biot coupling generate eps_yy = b*p/M even at nu=0, which halves the undrained pressure jump and adds b^2/M to the effective storage.

physical_groups.name: probe_x025
physical_groups._comment: PAPER_VALUE: evaluation point X=0.25 m (Fig. 4.1). dim-0 group -> exact mesh vertex at box centre.

physical_groups.name: probe_lhs
physical_groups._comment: lhs free boundary midpoint for displacement query

mesh._comment: recombine=true -> quads, REQUIRED for hydro_mechanical (upquad11). With a 0.1 m strip height this gives a STRUCTURED 200x2 grid of 400 quads - which also removes the unstructured corner patch that hosted the DSS dead-node failure (see ANALYSIS.md). Report's own mesh study (BGR, Figs. 4.2-4.3) showed ~256 elements converged, so 200 along the column is right. u-p monotonicity floor dt >= h^2/(6c) = 0.05^2/(6*5.09e-8) = 8.2e3 s at this h.

hydro_mechanical._comment: monolithic Biot u-p solve; no source/target fields by design

displacement._comment_nu: PAPER_VALUE: nu=0 by model definition - 1D model, transverse stresses vanish (Table 4.1, Sec. 2.2)
displacement._comment_rho: ASSUMED: 2000 kg/m3 generic geomaterial bulk density. REQUIRED by the hydro_mechanical builder. Quasi-static analysis -> zero impact on results.

pore_pressure._comment_perm: PAPER_VALUE: K=1e-20 m2 (Table 4.1) via the intrinsic_permeability route; viscosity 1e-9 MPa.s = 1e-3 Pa.s (Table 4.1). Pipeline computes mobility - never hand-converted.
pore_pressure._comment_storage: PAPER_VALUE: porosity 0.15, K_liquid 2100 MPa (Table 4.1); grains incompressible, consistent with b=1. Gives Q=K_f/n=14 GPa, 1/Q=7.14e-11 1/Pa.
pore_pressure._comment_sanity: c_v=(k/mu)/(1/Q+1/E)=5.09e-8 m2/s; fundamental time L^2/(pi^2 c_v)=6.3 a -> 30 a run reaches steady state, matching the report's profile schedule.

initial_conditions._comment: EXCESS pore pressure: paper IC p0=0.1013 MPa absolute (Table 4.1) is the datum -> 0 Pa excess. Zero consistent state, satisfying the backend IC admissibility rule.

boundary_conditions._comment: PAPER_VALUE: lhs pore pressure 1 MPa absolute (Table 4.1) -> 0.8987 MPa excess after datum shift. Drained, prescribed-pressure boundary.
PAPER_VALUE: rhs pore pressure 0.1013 MPa absolute = datum -> 0 Pa excess.

PAPER_VALUE: lhs total stress 1 MPa compressive (Table 4.1) -> increment 0.8987 MPa over the initial 0.1013 MPa equilibrium. Compression = +x traction on the left face (tension-positive FEM convention).

PAPER_VALUE (implicit): lateral confinement of the 1D column, eps_yy=0. Together with the edge_top constraint this makes the 2D plane-strain mapping exact. NOT merely rigid-body suppression - see metadata.notes.

PAPER_VALUE (implicit): the reference is a 1D oedometric column, eps_yy=0. Under Biot coupling a traction-free top gives eps_yy = b*p/M even at nu=0, which drops the undrained jump from 5.7181e5 to 3.4949e5 Pa and stretches the fundamental time from 6.31 a to 10.32 a. Not optional.

time_stepping._comment_t_end: PAPER_VALUE: last profile time 30 a (Sec. 4.1.1) = 30*365.25*86400 s
time_stepping._comment_linear_solver: MUST stay skyline. linear_solver 'dss' maps hydro_mechanical (symmetric_tangent=True) onto SMT_DSS_sym_LDL, an UNPIVOTED LDL^T, but the u-p tangent is symmetric INDEFINITE (a saddle point). It breaks down on the LAST equation of the system - node 2835's P_f in the v5 mesh - and leaves that pressure DOF dead at p~0, i.e. a spurious point sink. Controlled test (2026-08-17, same mesh, same config, 3 steps): node 2834 p = -3.289e-07 under dss vs 657831 Pa under skyline, max|dp| over all 2835 nodes = 6.578e5 attained at exactly that node, displacements agreeing to 2.2e-6 m. In the v5 run that one node stole 15.6% of the inlet flux and scaled the whole steady profile to 0.844x. The v5 comment reasoned against the WRONG caveat: solver.py documents only DSS's accuracy floor on free/unloaded problems, which is a different failure mode. Skyline was 65 s/step at 8505 unknowns; the 0.05 m strip (v6) drops that to ~1200 unknowns, so cost is no longer a reason to reach for dss.
time_stepping._comment_dt: log grid sums to 30 a. dt_min raised 1e3 -> 6e3 s in v5 to clear the upquad11 (unstabilised equal-order u-p) monotonicity floor dt >= h^2/(6c) = 0.0415^2/(6*5.09e-8) = 5.6e3 s; at dt_min=1e3 the first step rang on both boundaries (p oscillating 898700/131927/392615/320900 near x=0, 29 nodes undershooting the interior plateau). Still ~16 steps before the report's first profile instant at 0.003 a = 9.47e4 s. If finer early resolution is ever needed, refine h near the boundaries instead - the floor scales as h^2.

reference_curves.label: Analytical X=0.25m
reference_curves._comment: Digitised from Fig. 4.8 (log time axis); Fig. 4.7 is the SAME data on a linear axis, so one set serves both evolution plots. ABSOLUTE MPa vs years - the report's own units. Provenance and verification: reference/README.md.

reference_curves.label: Analytical steady state
reference_curves._comment: Fig. 4.11 draws ONE analytical curve (the steady state). The transient reference for u(x) is the 8-code band below.

reference_curves.label: Analytical steady state (repo)
reference_curves._comment: u_mm -> m via y_scale. Independently computed, agrees with the digitised Fig. 4.11 curve to 2.3e-4 mm.

queries.label: p'(x) profile
queries._comment: No at_time, so the last step (30 a) is what source:'query' plots. The earlier instants are the p_prof_* snapshots below.

queries.label: lhs displacement [m]
queries._comment: Renamed from u_lhs_mm: the query returns METRES, the old id said mm. Expect +5.617e-4 m at steady state.

queries.label: p at X=0.25m [MPa abs]
queries._comment: excess Pa -> absolute MPa, the units the report's figures are plotted in.

queries.label: u(x) profile
queries._comment: Was missing entirely - Fig. 4.11 had nothing to compare against. No at_time: last step = 30 a.

queries.label: p(x) at 0.003a
queries._comment: The report's profile instants (Figs 4.10/4.11). at_time fires once, on the step crossing it. 30 a is deliberately NOT an at_time query: t_end is exactly 30 a, so no step would cross it - p_profile/u_profile cover it.

plots.name: pw_evolution_log
plots.title: Pore-water pressure at the 5 probes (log time) - Fig. 4.8
plots._comment: Mirrors Fig. 4.8. THE diagnostic plot: the reported early-time discrepancy (interior jump 3.50e5 instead of 5.72e5 Pa, diffusivity off by 1+Q/E=2.75) lives at t<0.1 a and is invisible on a linear axis. Digitised curves start at t=1e-3 a - the log axis' left edge.

plots._comment: Mirrors Fig. 4.7 (same data as 4.8, linear time axis).
